The budget tracker is built and covers all 11 requirements. The 18 unit tests pass, the browser test passes at 1280px and 375px, and type-check, lint and the production build come back clean. I haven't committed anything.

**How it works**
- **Exact amounts:** money is parsed from the text you type straight into whole cents and summed as whole numbers, so 0.1 + 0.2 shows 0.30. Amounts with more than two decimal places are rejected rather than rounded.
- **Main code:** the logic (validation, totals, filters, CSV, saving) is in `src/lib/money.ts` and `src/lib/budget.ts`. The interface is in `src/App.tsx`, and the donut chart is a hand-drawn SVG in `src/components/Donut.tsx`.
- **Budgets:** each category has one monthly limit that applies to every month. It shows a bar and "X left", or a red bar and "Over budget by X".
- **Months:** if you add a transaction dated in another month, the app switches to that month and tells you, so the entry doesn't seem to vanish.
- **Deleting:** asks you to confirm in the row itself ("Delete" / "Keep").
- **CSV export:** contains all of the selected month's transactions, even when filters are on. Quotes and commas are handled, and notes starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` get a leading `'` so spreadsheets don't run them as formulas.
- **Saving:** if browser storage is unreadable or corrupt the app starts with defaults instead of crashing, and if a save fails you see a warning banner.
- **New tooling:** I added `vitest` as a dev dependency, plus `npm test` (unit tests) and `npm run test:e2e` (browser tests) scripts.

Recurring transactions are working. All 41 unit tests pass, and all 4 browser tests pass: the original app walkthrough and the new recurring one, each at 1280px and 375px. Lint and the production build are clean, and I haven't committed anything.

**How it works**
- **Repeat monthly:** a checkbox in the add/edit form. The hint underneath says when it will repeat, for example "every later month on the 31st (or the last day in shorter months)".
- **Copies are real transactions:** each month's copy is a normal transaction, so it counts in totals, the chart, budgets and CSV export. Repeating rows show a "↻ Monthly" badge.
- **No duplicates:** each repeating transaction remembers the last month it has filled in. Opening a later month fills in every month up to it, including any you skipped, and never fills a month twice. Reopening a month or reloading adds nothing, and a single copy you delete stays deleted.
- **Short months:** the 31st becomes the 30th, the 28th, or the 29th in leap years.
- **Recurring screen:** a new tab next to "Overview" with an active-count badge. It lists every repeating transaction with its day, amount, months covered, and Active or Stopped.
  - "Stop…" lets you pick the first month it should no longer appear in, and tells you what happens: "May 2026 and earlier stay as they are. 21 transactions from June 2026 on will be removed."
  - A stopped one can be stopped earlier, but not pushed later.

**Choices I made where the spec was open**
- **Editing a copy that still repeats:** the change applies to that month and all later months; earlier months keep their old values. Moving it to a different month is blocked with a clear message. You can still change the day.
- **Unticking "Repeat monthly" while editing:** this copy is kept as a one-off and the repeat stops from that month on.
- **Ticking it on an existing one-off:** that transaction becomes the first month of a new repeating transaction.
- **Stopping from the very first month:** the repeating transaction and all its copies are removed, so it leaves the list.
- **Export button moved on mobile:** on mobile, "Export CSV" moved from the header into the Transactions card to make room for the tabs. On desktop it's still in the header.

The Kanban board is built and all 11 requirements work at 1280px and 375px. Both test suites pass: 28 unit tests for the logic, and 18 browser tests in real Chrome. Typecheck and lint are clean. Nothing is committed yet.

**How it works**
- **Dragging:** I wrote it myself rather than adding a library, so the same code handles mouse, touch and pen. With a mouse you can drag a card from anywhere on it. On touch you drag from the dotted handle on the left edge, so touching the rest of the card still scrolls the page. The page scrolls on its own when you drag near the top or bottom edge, and Escape cancels a drag.
- **Keyboard:** each card has a "Move to…" dropdown. If you Tab to a card, Shift+←/→ moves it to the next column, Shift+↑/↓ moves it up or down in its column, and focus stays on the card. A screen reader announces the card's new position.
- **Work-in-progress limit:** Doing shows "n / 3". When it has more than 3 cards, the column turns amber and shows a warning. You can still add the fourth card; it only warns.
- **Search and filter:** while a search or priority filter is on, column counts show "shown/total". Dragging cards still drops them in the right place while the board is filtered.
- **Saving:** the board is saved to localStorage in a versioned format. If the saved data is damaged, the app drops the bad entries instead of crashing. Changes made in another tab show up in this one.

The Markdown notes app is built, and all 12 requirements pass in a real Chrome browser at both 1280px and 375px wide. **How it works**
- **Markdown rendering:** I wrote a small renderer (`src/lib/markdown.ts`) instead of adding a library.
  - **Safety:** it escapes all of the note's text and only outputs tags it creates itself, so raw HTML in a note shows up as plain text. Links are only kept if they're web, email or phone links (or relative), so `javascript:` links are dropped.
  - **Checkboxes:** each one records which line of the note it came from, so clicking it in the preview flips the `[ ]`/`[x]` on that line.
- **Layout:** on desktop the note list, editor and preview sit side by side. On mobile you see the note list first; tapping a note opens the editor with the preview below it, and a back button returns to the list.
- **Rename and delete:** you rename a note by editing its title at the top of the editor. Delete asks for confirmation in a dialog (Cancel, Escape or clicking outside it all cancel).
- **Saving:** notes save automatically 0.4 seconds after you stop typing, and the indicator shows "Saving…" then "Saved". Anything not yet saved is also written when the page closes, so reloading right after typing loses nothing. If browser storage is full, the indicator says the note wasn't saved.
- **Sorting:** pinning a note doesn't count as editing it, so it doesn't change the "last edited" order.
- **First visit:** a "Welcome" note demonstrating the features is created.

Tags are working. Any `#tag` in a note's text becomes a tag. The sidebar lists every tag with its note count, and you can filter by a tag, rename it everywhere, and get suggestions while typing. All 64 logic tests and all 30 browser tests pass, and lint and the type-check are clean. I haven't committed anything.

**How tags behave**
- **What counts as a tag:** `#` followed by letters, digits, `_` or `-`, like `#work`, `#to-do` or `#zażółć`. Tags ignore case and are shown in lowercase.
- **What doesn't count:**
  - `# Heading` (a hash followed by a space)
  - numbers like `#42`
  - `C#`, `page#anchor` and URLs
  - anything inside code
- **Sidebar:** a "Tags" section shows each tag with how many notes use it. Clicking a tag filters the list, and clicking it again clears the filter. A bar ("Tagged #work · Rename · ×") also has a clear button. The tag filter combines with search.
- **Preview:** tags appear as small chips, and clicking one filters the list too (on mobile it switches back to the list).
- **Suggestions while typing:** typing `#` lists existing tags. Tags that start with what you've typed come first, then tags that contain it. Arrow keys move through the list, Enter, Tab or a click inserts the tag plus a space, and Escape closes it, so Enter then makes a normal new line. The list doesn't appear in code or after `# ` for a heading.
- **Rename:** choose Rename in the filter bar, then type a new name. Every note's text is updated, but only whole tags: renaming `#work` doesn't touch `#workshop`, `#work-items` or anything inside code. Invalid names show an error. Renaming to a tag that already exists warns you first, then merges the two. Renamed notes count as edited, so they move to the top of the list.

The bill-splitting app is built and meets all 11 requirements. The logic tests, the browser tests at 1280px and 375px, typecheck, build and lint all pass. Run it with `npm run dev` and open http://localhost:5211. I haven't committed anything.

**How it works and choices I made**
- **Rounding:** all money is stored in whole cents. Shared items, tax and tip are each split by the largest-remainder method, so the per-person totals always add up exactly to the bill total. When an item doesn't divide evenly, the leftover cent goes to a different person on each item, not always the same one.
- **Tax and tip** are both calculated on the items subtotal (before tax), then split in proportion to what each person ordered. The page says this under the tax and tip fields.
- **Removing a person** who is the only one on an item is blocked, with a message naming the item. Otherwise that item would be left with nobody.
- **Duplicate names** are rejected (ignoring case).
- **Price and percentage fields** accept a comma as the decimal separator (e.g. "12,50"), allow at most 2 decimal places for prices, and reject negative numbers and text that isn't a number. Each field shows its own error message.
- **Currency formatting:** USD shows `$1,234.56`, EUR `1.234,56 €` and PLN `1234,56 zł`. Polish style doesn't group four-digit amounts, so `12 345,67 zł` is the first grouped case.
- **Reset** asks for confirmation in a dialog. It clears everything except the selected currency.
- **Reload:** the bill is saved to localStorage on every change. Corrupt or malformed saved data falls back to an empty bill instead of crashing.

The logic is in `src/lib/bill.ts` and the UI in `src/App.tsx`. I added `vitest` as a dev dependency, plus `npm test` and `npm run e2e` scripts.

  - Bill totals, plus 500 random bills checking that the per-person totals reconcile.

**How it behaves**
- **Timer:** the clock stores the time the current phase ends, not a count of ticks. The screen recomputes from that whenever it updates, and again when you come back to the tab, so time spent in the background doesn't throw it off. A phase that ended while you were away (or while the page was closed) still gets logged with the time it actually ended.
- **Phases:** when a phase ends, the next one is set up but waits for you to press Start.
  - Skipping a focus session doesn't count toward the 4 dots and doesn't add a log entry.
  - The dots reset to zero after the long break.
- **Space bar:** starts and pauses, but not while you're typing in the task box or the settings. If a button has keyboard focus, Space still toggles the timer once rather than also pressing that button.
- **Settings:** each duration must be a whole number from 1 to 90. Errors show inline and Save stays disabled until all three are valid. New durations take effect right away if the timer isn't running; a running or paused session keeps its original length.
- **Saved data:** settings, today's log, the mute setting, the task label and the timer itself are saved in localStorage, so a reload doesn't lose a session in progress. Entries from earlier days are dropped.
- **Design:** warm terracotta for focus, sage green for short breaks and slate blue for the long break, with a progress ring around the countdown and a single column that fits a phone.

Repeating monthly transactions are in. The new logic tests (34 in total now) and 4 browser tests, 2 at each width, all pass, and `tsc` and `oxlint` are clean.

**How it behaves**
- **Repeat monthly:** the add/edit dialog has a "Repeat monthly" checkbox. Ticking it on a new or an existing transaction makes it repeat.
- **Later months:** a repeating transaction appears in each later month when you open it, on the same day. A rule set on the 31st gives Feb 28 (29 in leap years), Apr 30 and Mar 31 again. Opening a month again, or reloading, never creates a second copy.
- **Recurring screen:** a new "Recurring" tab lists every repeating transaction with its day, start month and status. "Stop from [month]" asks you to confirm. Months before the chosen one stay unchanged; that month and later ones lose their copies. Stopped rules stay listed as "Stopped from …".
- **Marker:** repeating transactions show a ↻ in the list.

**Choices I made where you didn't specify**
- **Editing one month:** editing an occurrence changes only that month. To change the amount for future months, stop the rule and add a new one.
- **Unticking the box:** unticking "Repeat monthly" on an occurrence stops the rule from the next month on. Re-ticking it on the last occurrence resumes the rule.
- **Deleting one month:** deleting one occurrence removes only that month's copy, and it doesn't come back when you reopen the month.
- **Months you skip:** only the month you open gets its copy, so skipped months aren't back-filled. Each month's totals don't depend on the others, so nothing is lost.

Tags are in, and everything passes: 31 logic tests and 6 browser runs at 1280px and 375px.

**How it works**
- **What counts as a tag:** a `#tag` in a note's text, case-insensitive and stored lowercase. A heading like `# Title`, text in code, URL fragments and `abc#def` are not tags.
- **Sidebar:** a Tags section lists each tag with its note count, sorted by name. The section only appears once some note has a tag.
- **Filtering:** clicking a tag filters the list, and clicking it again clears the filter. It combines with search, and it clears itself if the tag no longer exists.
- **Suggestions:** typing `#` in the editor opens a popup of existing tags that start with what you've typed. Enter, Tab or a click inserts the tag plus a space, and the caret lands after it. The arrow keys move the highlight and Escape closes the popup. Enter is a normal newline when no popup is open. There are no suggestions in headings or code.
- **Renaming:** the ✎ button on a tag opens an inline input; Enter or Save applies it and Escape cancels. It rewrites every occurrence in every note's text, matching case-insensitively. An invalid name shows an error. The active filter follows the new name, and renaming to an existing tag merges the two.

**One bug fixed along the way:** the browser's selection event fires after typing and was resetting the highlighted suggestion, so ArrowDown then Enter could pick the wrong tag. It now resets only when the typed text changes.

**Known quirk:** while you type `#wo`, the partial tag briefly shows up in the sidebar until you finish or delete it.

**How it works**
- **Rounding:** all money is whole cents. Each item is split among its sharers, then tax and tip are divided in proportion to each person's items. Leftover cents go to whoever has the largest remainder, so the per-person totals always add up exactly to the bill total.
- **Orphaned items:** removing a person who was the only sharer of an item leaves that item with nobody assigned. It is left out of the totals and a warning tells you to edit it.
- **Price rule:** prices must be greater than zero. Zero is rejected, not just negatives.
- **Currency formatting:** USD uses `$1,234.56`, EUR uses `1.234,56 €`, and PLN uses `1 234,56 zł`.

How it behaves:
- **History:** the app already kept every completed session in `localStorage`. Each session now also records its minutes, and sessions saved before this change count as 25 minutes each.
- **This week** means the last 7 days including today, the same days the chart shows.
- **Streak:** consecutive days with at least one completed session. If you haven't finished one yet today, yesterday's streak still counts until the day ends.
- **Space bar:** it starts and pauses only on the Timer tab. On Stats it does nothing, so you can't change a hidden timer by accident.
- **Export CSV:** a file named `pomodoro-sessions-YYYY-MM-DD.csv` with columns Date, Time, Task, Minutes, oldest first. It is disabled when there are no sessions. Task labels starting with `=`, `+`, `-` or `@` get a leading `'` so spreadsheets don't read them as formulas.
